inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Give the skill increment an interpretive anchor and bridge it to the standardised and population-level percentage contrasts
inherited_criterion.letter_text: The Discussion and Abstract explicitly relate the skill increment to at least one patient-scale or benchmark quantity reported in the paper.

operationalization.fully_addressed: The Discussion contains an interpretive passage, and the Abstract at least one sentence, that explicitly relate the size of the social-position log-loss skill increment (0.42 to 1.37 points in round 1, or the revised values) to patient-scale or benchmark quantities reported in the paper: the standardised area and marital percentage-point contrasts and the population-level 'all social features as observed' contrast (or, additionally, a benchmark increment such as the year or treatment-type increment), and explain how skill points and these percentage contrasts relate, so a health services reader can judge whether the increment is large or small. Calling the increment 'small but informative' without naming a reported comparator does not count.
operationalization.partially_addressed: A bridge exists in only one of Discussion and Abstract; or the quantities are placed next to each other without saying how they relate; or the increment is related to only one of the standardised and population-level contrasts.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: The revision describes the increment's practical importance more strongly (for example 'substantial', 'meaningful') without any stated comparator, introduces a bridge that misstates reported values, or removes comparisons that the round-1 text already made.

Keeping the example only as an illustration that small gains occur, with the argument carried by other reasoning, is acceptable.

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: State the conditioning on recorded curative treatment in the abstract and Conclusions; carry "not evidence of better care" forward; say the bounds do not cover selection into the treated cohort and discuss bias direction for area measures
inherited_criterion.letter_text: The Abstract Conclusions and Conclusions name the recorded-curative-treatment population, and the Discussion states the scope of the bounds.

operationalization.fully_addressed: (a) The Abstract Conclusions and the Conclusions section name the conditioning population, men with recorded curative treatment (radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy), in or next to the direction statement; (b) the Conclusions carry the qualifier that shorter recorded waits are not evidence of better care; (c) the Discussion states that the selection bounds cover only men without a recorded interval and not selection into the recorded-curative-treatment cohort; and (d) the Discussion discusses the likely direction of this selection bias for the area measures (rurality and income) as well as marital status, which may include stating that the direction cannot be identified and why.
operationalization.partially_addressed: Some but not all of (a) to (d) are met, for example the population is named in the Conclusions but not the Abstract, or the bounds' scope is stated but bias direction for area measures is not discussed.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: The direction statement is extended to all diagnosed men or to access in general, the bounds are described as covering treatment selection, or the 'not evidence of better care' qualifier is removed from the Discussion.

items.expected_change_surface: Abstract Conclusions; Conclusions; Discussion (The rural direction, Marital status, selection and limitations)

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: State that 98 of 100 refers to intervals, and note the 0.00 lower bound

operationalization.fully_addressed: The Abstract (and any repeat of the count) says that it is the 95% intervals that stayed above 0 in 98 of 100 scenario, stratum and model results (point estimates being above 0 in all), and notes that one of the counted lower bounds is 0.00 (180-day threshold, unknown risk, penalised logistic regression). If re-analysis changes the count, the revised count is stated with the same interval wording and any boundary lower bound is noted.

items.expected_change_surface: Abstract (Results sentence 'stayed above 0 in 98 of 100 results'); Results, Sensitivity analyses

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Qualify the "triage" reading: state that higher-risk radiotherapy patients often start hormone therapy first; bring the prostatectomy-only gradient into the main text; report the clinical-need increment for that scenario
inherited_criterion.letter_text: The main text reports the prostatectomy-only gradient and clinical-need increment, and "triage" is presented as one possible explanation.

operationalization.fully_addressed: (a) The manuscript states, in Outcome or Interpretation, that men with higher-risk disease treated with radiotherapy often start androgen deprivation therapy before radiotherapy, so the recorded interval may end at hormone therapy; (b) the main text, not only the supplement, reports the prostatectomy-only risk gradient in delay (in round 1, low risk 45.8% and high risk 38.4% against 47.9% and 32.8% in the primary analysis, a gap of 7.4 against 15.1 points); (c) the main text reports the clinical-need increment for the prostatectomy-only scenario; and (d) 'triage' is presented as one possible explanation among several, not as the finding.
operationalization.partially_addressed: Some but not all of (a) to (d) are met, for example the hormone therapy caveat is added and triage hedged, but the prostatectomy-only gradient or its clinical-need increment is not in the main text.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: The triage reading is stated more strongly or spreads to new places (for example the Abstract), or the Methods statement that the interval ends at the first treatment of any kind is removed.

items.expected_change_surface: Methods, Outcome; Discussion, Interpretation and Principal findings; Conclusions; Results (sensitivity analyses, main text)

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Correct the "clinical information only" risk-group sentence; state that regional stage is often pathological for surgical men; consider a step 1 sensitivity analysis without stage
inherited_criterion.letter_text: The Methods no longer describe risk groups as clinical-only, and the treatment of stage in step 1 is stated for the primary and Gleason-and-PSA-only analyses.

operationalization.fully_addressed: The Methods no longer say risk groups use clinical information only; they state that regional summary stage is often pathological for men treated surgically; and they state whether stage is included in step 1 for the primary analysis and for the Gleason-and-PSA-only analysis. A step 1 sensitivity analysis without stage is optional under this criterion ('consider'); its presence or absence does not change the verdict.
operationalization.partially_addressed: The 'clinical information only' sentence is corrected but the pathological nature of stage for surgical men, or the treatment of stage in step 1 for both analyses, is not stated.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: The revision newly asserts that risk groups or the step 1 block are purely pre-treatment clinical information, or removes the existing limitation that summary stage partly uses surgical pathology.

items.expected_change_surface: Methods, Clinical risk groups; Methods, Ordered feature steps; sensitivity analysis description (Gleason-and-PSA-only scenario)

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Remove or qualify "lower is better" labels, especially for low-risk men; state once that a longer wait is not necessarily worse care

operationalization.fully_addressed: The 'lower is better' (and similar 'fewer is better') labels in the Abstract, Results and figure legends are removed or qualified, and in any case are not applied to low-risk men without qualification; and the manuscript states at least once that a longer wait is not necessarily worse care.

items.expected_change_surface: Abstract Results; Results; figure legends and axes (for example Figure 2); Discussion, Interpretation

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Say "recorded clinical variables, which vary little within this group by definition" for the low-risk comparison

operationalization.fully_addressed: Wherever the low-risk comparison of social position with clinical need appears (Abstract, Discussion), clinical need is qualified as the recorded clinical variables, which vary little within the low-risk group by definition (this wording or equivalent meaning), or the comparison is removed.

items.expected_change_surface: Abstract Results; Discussion, Principal findings (low-risk comparison of social position with clinical need)

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Present the active-surveillance exclusion as an assumption; cite the coding rule; report the share of intervals over 365 days and top-coded, by risk group

operationalization.fully_addressed: The Methods present the exclusion of men on active surveillance as an assumption that depends on SEER first-course coding rather than a certainty, cite the SEER coding rule for first course of treatment, and report by risk group the share of intervals over 365 days and the share top-coded (731 days or more).

items.expected_change_surface: Methods, Active surveillance; supplementary table of interval distribution by risk group

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Restrict the Huang et al. [22] claim to favourable-risk disease; use its rural surveillance finding in the selection discussion

operationalization.fully_addressed: The citation of Huang et al. (SEER study of favourable-risk men, low and favourable intermediate risk) is restricted to favourable-risk disease rather than supporting findings pooled across intermediate and high risk, and its finding that rural low-risk men were more likely to be on surveillance or watchful waiting is used where the manuscript discusses selection into the treated cohort.

items.expected_change_surface: Discussion, Marital status; Discussion passage on selection into the treated cohort

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Give the scope of Noone's 80% figure and carry its caution into the secondary-outcome interpretation

operationalization.fully_addressed: The sentence citing Noone et al. (Med Care) for 80% radiation sensitivity states its scope, namely a Medicare-linked older population with the figure pooled across several cancer sites and varying by site, stage and patient characteristics; and the interpretation of the secondary outcome (recorded curative treatment by social group or rurality) carries Noone's caution against using SEER treatment fields to compare treated with untreated people.

items.expected_change_surface: Limitations (Noone 80% sensitivity sentence); Results and Discussion interpretation of the secondary outcome

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Replace "corresponds to" with candidate-analogue wording in Supplementary Box 2; avoid "remote" for US counties

operationalization.fully_addressed: Supplementary Box 2 no longer says the Rural-Urban Continuum Code (or county income) 'corresponds to' the Australian measure and uses candidate-analogue or proxy wording instead; and US counties are not called 'remote' (for example nonmetropolitan counties not adjacent to a metropolitan area).

items.expected_change_surface: Supplementary Box 2; Results and tables terminology for US county categories

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Attribute the waiting-time paradox to [10] and the triage explanation to the authors or a prostate-specific source

operationalization.fully_addressed: The Introduction attributes to Ang et al. only the waiting-time paradox (unadjusted lower mortality with longer intervals, pooled across cancers), and attributes the explanation that aggressive disease is treated sooner either to the authors' own inference or to a prostate-specific source that reports it.

items.expected_change_surface: Introduction (waiting-time paradox sentence citing Ang et al.)

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Set the metropolitan direction and the 2010 to 2022 rise against evidence on large centres and time trends (e.g. Khorana 2019)

operationalization.fully_addressed: The Discussion sets both the metropolitan (large-centre) direction and the 2010 to 2022 rise in delay (36.0% to 52.3% in round 1) against published evidence on large or academic centres and on time trends in time to treatment, such as Khorana et al. 2019 (PLoS One, NCDB) or an equivalent source.

items.expected_change_surface: Discussion, The rural direction; Discussion interpretation of the 2010 to 2022 trend

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Name the SEER variables for clinical Gleason score and PSA in the manuscript

operationalization.fully_addressed: The manuscript names the SEER variables (field or recode names) used for clinical Gleason score and for PSA.

items.expected_change_surface: Methods, Clinical risk groups (or a variable definition table referenced from Methods)

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Rename or qualify "social position" in the title, abstract and Conclusions; state prominently that two of three variables are ecological and that registry differences load onto the block
inherited_criterion.letter_text: Title, Abstract and Conclusions either use the renamed label or qualify "social position" with its ecological and registry content.

operationalization.fully_addressed: In the title, Abstract and Conclusions, the block is either renamed (for example area and marital attributes) or 'social position' is qualified wherever it appears with its ecological and registry content; and the manuscript states prominently (for example in the Abstract or where the block is first defined, not only in Methods Uncertainty or Limitations) that two of the three variables, county rurality and county income, are ecological area measures and that unmeasured registry differences load onto the block.
operationalization.partially_addressed: The label is renamed or qualified in only some of title, Abstract and Conclusions, or the ecological and registry statement is present only in a non-prominent place such as Methods Uncertainty or Limitations.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: The label is strengthened towards individual socioeconomic position (for example 'socioeconomic status' or 'social disadvantage'), or the existing registry-differences caveat is removed.

items.expected_change_surface: Title; Abstract; Conclusions; Methods definition of the social block

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Report excess waiting days per man, the top-coded share, and why the 7-day threshold could not be applied

operationalization.fully_addressed: The manuscript reports excess waiting days per man (not only per 1,000 men), the share of excess days attributable to top-coded intervals (731 days or more), and states that the protocol's pre-specified 7-day meaningful difference could not be applied and why.

operationalization.fully_addressed: Where the Discussion restates the Foley et al. 2025 Tasmanian public-private difference (42 to 59 days), it restricts it to men not treated with external beam radiotherapy.
